name: Hadal-Glen
description: A shell of ancient ice seals the world, cracked into plates the size of nations and refrozen in place. Pressure ridges stack in turquoise ramparts, gleaming under a stingy sun near a nearby asteroid belt.

There is a hush that is not emptiness but attention, as if the landscape were listening back. Visitors report dreams of falling that persist for days after departure. Mats of pigment-bearing microbes stain the wet stone in bands of rust and violet.
Instruments disagree about the temporal distortion zone: mass reads one value, inertia another. Probes sent in return transmitting their own launch signals, timestamped hours early.
There is money in dark crystals here, and history in the rocks, and the two keep interfering with each other. Mediators do brisk business at inflated rates.
